title: Quantum-Enhanced Matterwave Interferometry in a Ring Waveguide
abstract: We propose a quantum-enhanced matter-wave interferometry protocol based on fractional-revival dynamics of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a ring, combined with a controlled interaction quench. Using the Truncated Wigner Approximation, we show that nonlinear evolution to the quarter revival generates modest spin squeezing of $-2.03\pm0.28\;$dB, which subsequently degrades under further nonlinear evolution. In contrast, starting from a non-interacting condensate, a controlled interaction quench applied after the initial quarter-revival beam-splitter operation generates substantially stronger spin squeezing of $-14.57\pm0.27\;$dB. We further show that phase control at $t=3T_r/8$ rotates the squeezed quadrature onto the phase-sensitive direction $\hat{J}_y$, producing a phase-squeezed state at $t=T_r/2$. The subsequent quarter-revival evolution converts this phase-squeezed state into a number-squeezed state, enabling population-difference readout. The resulting sequence provides a route to quantum-enhanced interferometry using the intrinsic fractional-revival dynamics of a ring together with controlled interaction and phase operations.
summary: The authors propose a novel quantum-enhanced matter-wave interferometer using a BEC in a ring waveguide. They leverage the intrinsic fractional-revival dynamics combined with controlled interaction quenching to generate significant spin squeezing. This method provides a robust, all-matter-wave route for high-precision quantum sensing.
main_problem: Developing a quantum-enhanced matter-wave interferometry protocol that utilizes the intrinsic dynamics of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) in a ring waveguide.
main_result: The proposed protocol achieves substantially stronger spin squeezing ($-14.57 \pm 0.27 	ext{ dB}$) by incorporating a controlled interaction quench after the initial fractional-revival beam-splitter operation.
method: The analysis employs the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) to model the nonlinear evolution and quantum fluctuations within the BEC.
model_or_system: The system is a Bose-Einstein condensate confined to a ring waveguide. The dynamics are governed by the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, analyzed through the lens of fractional-revival (FR) dynamics.
key_observables: Spin squeezing (measured in dB), condensate fraction ($ ar{\lambda}(t)$), and phase coherence ($c(t)$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($g$), revival time ($T_r$), and specific time points for phase control ($t=3T_r/8$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) and, in one derivation, assumes negligible spatial overlap between modes during nonlinear evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the probability density and phase evolution during fractional revival, showing the shift of revival peaks with nonlinearity, and tracking the condensate fraction and phase coherence over time.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical basis using BEC dynamics in a ring, detailing the role of fractional revival. It then develops a protocol involving phase control and controlled interaction quenching to generate spin squeezing, culminating in the demonstration of quantum-enhanced interferometry.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum metrology using ultracold atoms, showing how intrinsic quantum dynamics (FR) can replace external optical components while achieving squeezing below the Standard Quantum Limit.
